results.summary: This Wokwi project implements a simple combinational logic circuit that converts the ASCII binary representation of the letter 'A' (0x37) to the letter 'V' (0x56). The design is described as 'basic (broken) logic', suggesting it may not function correctly. The documentation is minimal, providing only a brief description and a test procedure. External hardware includes a DIP switch for inputs and a 7-segment display for outputs.

This design implements a WS2812 LED driver that converts an SPI input stream into the single-wire WS2812 protocol. It includes auxiliary functions such as PWM, UART, WS2812 waveform generation, LFSR, frequency counting, and ultrasonic distance sensing, implemented as space and time permit. The design is tested by using SPI to read and write registers and observing the LED display or serial response. External hardware includes an SPI master, WS2812 LEDs, and possibly a serial terminal.

This Wokwi project uses simple logic gates to display the letter 'P' on a 7-segment display when the 8-bit input equals 0x46. The design requires external hardware including a breadboard, 1.8V power supply, connector wires, an 8-position DIP switch, and a 7-segment display. The documentation is minimal, describing only the basic function and test procedure. The design is a simple combinational logic demonstration.

This Wokwi project implements a 'secret code' detector that outputs the letter 'r' on a 7-segment display when the input bits 10101010 are set on IN0 through IN7. The design requires external hardware including a DIP switch for inputs and a 7-segment display for outputs. The documentation is minimal, describing only the basic function and test procedure. The design is a simple combinational logic demonstration.

This Wokwi project implements a shift register with LED and 7-segment display outputs, controlled by a clock generator. The design requires external hardware including a clock source, a button, and a 7-segment LED display. The documentation is minimal, describing only the basic function and test procedure. The design is a simple sequential logic demonstration.

This Verilog design converts a 7-LED APA102 (SPI-style) data stream to a WS2812-compatible single-wire output. The design removes the first 8 bits of each 32-bit pixel value to handle the APA102 header. It is tested by sending SPI data and observing the WS2812 LED output. External hardware includes an SPI master and WS2812 LEDs.

External hardware includes buttons for inputs and an LED for output. The documentation is minimal, describing only the basic function and test procedure.
